header.label: OpenAEC Ecosystem
header.desc: The Everything-app for your business — email, ERP, invoices, time tracking, projects, communication and more in a single tool. Multi-tenant: one account, multiple ERPNext instances.

explainer1.title: What is Y-app?
explainer1.intro: Y-app is not a chat tool and not a standalone ERP frontend. It's an "Everything-app" — a multi-tenant ERPNext workspace that bundles your entire business stack into a single web application. Email (IMAP/SMTP + Office 365), ERP (ERPNext), files (NextCloud), chat (Teams, NextCloud Talk, Telegram), calendar, an AI assistant (Claude) and dozens of business modules — all reachable from a single browser tab.
explainer1.li1: Multi-tenant — connect multiple ERPNext instances to a single Y-app account
explainer1.li2: Encrypted vault — credentials in a server-side SQLite database with AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations)
explainer1.li3: No browser tabs needed — switch between instances via in-app tabs, each with its own routing and session
explainer1.li4: Employer or employee mode — restrict modules per instance via a dropdown
explainer1.li5: Full NL/EN i18n — 1190+ translations, switchable at runtime

howitworks.title: How it works
howitworks.intro: Y-app runs on your own server (or via impertio.app). Self-signup, instance management and mode switching all happen inside the app — no IT tickets needed.

step1.title: Create a Y-app account
step1.desc: Self-signup with email and password. Bcrypt with 12 rounds, HttpOnly session cookies, session-scoped credential cache.

step2.title: Add ERPNext instances
step2.desc: For every company or client: URL, name, colour and credentials. Encrypted immediately in the server-side vault.

step3.title: Switch via in-app tabs
step3.desc: No browser tabs: switch between instances inside Y-app. Each tab keeps its own routing state, ERPNext session and cache.

step4.title: Employer or Employee mode
step4.desc: Switch per instance between the full module set (Employer) or a restricted set for staff (Employee).

explainer2.title: Multi-tenant and encrypted — not even the host can read your credentials
explainer2.intro: Y-app runs on a zero-knowledge principle for your ERPNext credentials. Every combination of email, ERPNext key and OAuth2 token is encrypted in a server-side SQLite vault with a master key that can only be decrypted with your Y-app password.
explainer2.li1: AES-256-GCM — authenticated encryption for every credential
explainer2.li2: PBKDF2-SHA256, 210,000 iterations — the current OWASP recommendation for key derivation
explainer2.li3: Master key file with mode 600 — readable only by the Y-app process
explainer2.li4: AsyncLocalStorage per request — credentials are never shared between users in the same Node process
explainer2.li5: Not even the host can see your data — without your login the vault is a blob of random bytes
explainer2.li6: One account, multiple companies — ideal for accountants, consultants, holdings and franchise organisations

medewerkers.title: Employees

jaarrekening.title: Annual accounts

liquiditeit.title: Liquidity

nextcloudfiles.title: NextCloud Files

wiki.title: Wiki

techstack.title: Technology
techstack.summary: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + TailwindCSS 4 on the frontend, Node.js 20 + Express 4 + WebSocket on the backend. Authentication via bcryptjs (12 rounds), HttpOnly cookies and AsyncLocalStorage for per-request credential scoping. Encryption with AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations), data in a SQLite database (WAL mode). Production runs under PM2, behind an nginx reverse proxy with TLS termination, WebSocket upgrade and static dist serving. Development via tsx --watch.
